summary: The pre-flight free-space guard never fires: check_free_space treats its <force> argument as a boolean with `[ "$force" ]`, but callers pass the string "0" when force is off (snapshot.sh line 22: FORCE="${BACKUP_FORCE:-0}"), and `[ "0" ]` is true, so a shortfall is always downgraded to a log line.
trigger: Run ./snapshot.sh (or run-backup.sh) with --force absent and BACKUP_FORCE unset onto an archive filesystem with less free space than `du -sk` of the source: the run logs "continuing anyway" and proceeds to fill the filesystem instead of dying with "not enough space".

summary: Staging cleanup was dropped: the base script paired `mktemp -d` with `trap 'rm -rf "$STAGE"' EXIT INT TERM`, but after the move to make_stage the only cleanup left is the `rmdir "$STAGE"` on the success path, so any failure or signal leaves the staging directory behind — and it now holds a full-size finished archive, because replication happens before the archive is published.
trigger: Any failing or interrupted run after tar completes — e.g. BACKUP_REMOTE set to a host that refuses the connection, or Ctrl-C / a cron timeout during replication — leaves $TMPDIR/snapshot.XXXXXX/<label>-<stamp>.tar.gz on disk. A nightly job against an unreachable replica fills /tmp with one full backup per night.

summary: Command injection into the replica: replicate() interpolates the archive name (derived from the operator-supplied --label) and BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR into a single string that ssh hands to a remote shell; the single quotes only look protective, because the value itself may contain a quote and close them.
trigger: ./run-backup.sh --label "nightly'; rm -rf ~; :'" with BACKUP_REMOTE set makes the remote shell run: mkdir -p '/srv/replica' && cat > '/srv/replica/nightly'; rm -rf ~; :'-<stamp>.tar.gz — i.e. `rm -rf ~` executes on the replica. The same works through a label in a config file or a cron entry.

summary: Manifest v2 added a leading label column and snapshot.sh, run-backup.sh and the README were all updated, but prune.sh still reads three fields, so `path` receives "<bytes>\t<archive-path>", fails the `[ -f "$path" ]` test, and every record is skipped — rotation silently stops happening.
trigger: ./run-backup.sh --label nightly with more than BACKUP_KEEP archives already present: prune logs "manifest points at a missing archive" and deletes nothing, so archives accumulate forever and the retention policy is never enforced.
